rail_guard.text: Merthyr Tydfil! End of the line, and not a metaphor. This is where the Taff Vale Railway opened in 1841, taking iron and coal down to Cardiff docks.
Trains back down the valley run all the way to Cardiff. Hold on to your hat: there's a tunnel and a lot of weather.

mer_mam.text: Merthyr people are the friendliest in Wales, and the most argumentative. They go together.
Cyfarthfa Park's lovely on a dry day. Go on, have a walk round the lake. You'll meet dippers, tits, and my sister, who feeds the swans out of spite.

mer_busker.text: (Humming 'Myfanwy' on the pavement.) You've caught me. Joseph Parry wrote it, a Merthyr man. It's about a girl who doesn't love him back. Typical Welsh love song.
Every choir in Wales sings it. They sing it at weddings, funerals, and half time.

mer_rising.text: Dic Penderyn's name is on half the pubs and a lot of the walls in this town. Merthyr doesn't forget its own.
They say he was innocent. Nearly two centuries on, people are still saying it, and the campaign for a pardon has never quite gone quiet.

mer_walker.text: Cyfarthfa Lake was dug to feed the ironworks' water wheels. Now it feeds the ducks.
The castle's much grander than the house the ironmaster needed. That was the idea. He wanted the workers to look up and see who was in charge.

then.text: I stand corrected. Don't tell Mr Crawshay. I'd be dismissed. He'd say it was pure Cyfarthfa spite.

else.text: Another gawper? That engine'll never go anywhere. Five hundred guineas says it breaks the rails before the first bend.
